pays significant financial compensation if they quit a postbrexit reset deal as part of negotiations with sir keir starmer brussels has included a termination clause that would require london to pay a high level of restitution if they chose to exit a proposed euuk veterinary agreement to remove brexit red tape for british food and drink exporters according to a draft text seen by the ft eu diplomats have dubbed the stipulation a farage clause that they said was designed to insure the bloc against the risk of reform uk leader nigel farage becoming prime minister and making good on his threat to reverse starmers attempted move closer to brussels the clause states that if either side pulls out it must pay compensation that would include the costs of setting up the infrastructure and equipment initial recruitment and training in order to set up the necessary border controls one eu diplomat said that it was a safety provision to provide stability and a deterrent for farage and co adding that brussels was looking to sign a deal that would endure past the current uk parliamentary term which ends in 2029 the eu wants an agreement longterm and not only until 2029 should a change happen at the next election they said starmer has made a veterinary or sanitary and phytosanitary sps agreement a crucial element of his plans to improve trading arrangements with brussels alongside a deal to relink the eu and uk carbon pricing schemes trade and industry groups have strongly advocated for such a deal that would remove almost all brexit red tape faced by exporters of agrifood products a 2024 study estimated a deal could boost uk food and drink exports by 22 per cent with reform uk significantly ahead of both labour and the conservatives in the polls eu diplomats said brussels was increasingly alive to the risk of its planned deals with starmer unravelling the eu text said that the uk would pay a fee to join the veterinary agreement based on a proportional share of the relevant agencies that administer the blocs border checks on plant and animal imports plus an extra 4 per cent of that amount as an additional participation fee the draft text which is subject to negotiation with the british government also requires the uk to dynamically align with and simultaneously apply any rules governing animal and plant products that are introduced by eu lawmakers in brussels nick thomassymonds starmers european relations minister has said that legislation to enable dynamic alignment should be in place by the end of this year with the deal operational by early to mid 2027 however both reform uk and the conservatives have promised to revoke such a deal arguing that it diluted british legal independence and betrayed a vital part of honouring the result of the 2016 vote to leave the eu reform uk told the ft that the party would reverse the sps deal that starmer was negotiating with the eu if they won power speaking in london on friday farage accused starmer of doing his best to give away our parliamentary sovereignty to give away our rights as voters kemi badenoch conservative leader has promised to reverse starmers terrible deal saying she could not accept any agreement with brussels that involved britain being subject to rulings by the european court of justice the european commission said it remains fully committed to the implementation of the actions agreed with the united kingdom at the summit in may 2025 uk government officials said it was standard for agreements to have contingencies for termination and they would apply equally to both parties a senior labour official said it was ironic that both reform and the conservatives which styled themselves as parties of free markets were promising to restore trade barriers if they won the the state of the nation a country of chasms to understand india today consider two images in one a data analyst in a bengaluru highrise adds to the historic wealth of the top 1 who now capture nearly a quarter of the nations income in another just miles away a mother in a government hospital watches her newborn die because an incubator is a luxury her family cannot afford this is not an accident of economics it is the direct outcome of political choices that have nurtured a brutal inequality while systematically weaponizing faith to fracture the very idea of india engineering an unequal state the scale of indias inequality is not just staggering it is engineered while the government has touted world bank figures to claim india is the fourth most equal country this is a statistical sleight of hand built on sand the claim uses consumptionbased data which vastly underestimates the riches of billionaires who save rather than spend their fortunes the reality measured by serious economists is stark the richest 10 of indians gobble up nearly 58 of the national income while the bottom 50 subsist on just 15 this chasm is no natural law it is the result of a political project consider healthcare the governments spending is among the lowest in the world forcing decent care to be a luxury good every year 63 million indians are pushed into poverty by medical costsalmost two people every second the states undertaxation of the ultrawealthy contrasted with its reliance on indirect taxes that crush the poor is a deliberate policy choice that funnels wealth upward the state apparatus itself has been reconfigured to enforce this new order as amnesty international has documented national financial and investigation agencies have been weaponized to crack down on civil society human rights defenders and opposition leaders the arrest of sitting chief ministers like arvind kejriwal and hemant soren by the enforcement directorate ahead of elections exemplifies how legal process is leveraged for political containment dissent is criminalized under draconian laws like the uapa used to imprison activists and intellectuals for years without trial religion as a political weapon the architecture of division if economic policy has built a nation of haves and havenots the political strategy to maintain power has been to turn religion into a weapon of mass polarization this is not a matter of rhetoric alone it is a structured campaign the ideology driving this is hindutva a hindu nationalist project that seeks to transform indias secular democracy into a majoritarian authoritarian hindu state its political vehicle is the ruling bharatiya janata party bjp with prime minister narendra modi as its most prominent face a fulltime member of its ideological parent the rashtriya swayamsevak sangh rss their method is to create a divisive binary of insider versus outsider sacralizing hindu identity for political gain this strategy manifests in devastatingly concrete ways laws like the citizenship amendment act caa which excludes muslims legitimize discrimination on the basis of religion fundamentally altering the secular character of citizenship states have passed anticonversion laws described by critics as draconian tools to target and intimidate minorities and stifle religious freedom these laws are not abstract they create a climate of impunity violence and punitive justice communal violence has surged in 2024 alone india saw an alarming 84 rise in such violence this violence is often followed by a chilling form of extrajudicial punishment the bulldozing of homes and shops belonging primarily to muslims the supreme court itself has condemned these demolitions as collective punishment and unconstitutional statesanctioned exclusion from states suspending land sales between different religious communities to directives targeting muslimowned food businesses the state machinery is increasingly used to segregate and marginalize the institutional march the inauguration of the ram temple in ayodhya built on the site of the demolished babri masjid was not just a religious event but a powerful political symbol of this triumphalism coupled with the rewriting of school textbooks to erase lessons on democracy and secularism the project is clear to reshape the nations past present and future in a majoritarian image the human toll in the crossfire the cost is measured in human lives and a poisoned society it is measured in the 219 million indian children under five who are wasted severely underweight a number that shames a 3trillion economy it is measured in the mob lynchings the public demonization and the routine harassment of minorities it is measured in the fear that silences universities chokes journalism and turns activists into antinationals the 2024 election which denied the bjp a singleparty majority showed the limits of this strategy and offered a glimmer of resistance but the architecture of division and inequality remains firmly in place the state has not merely allowed these chasms to exist its policies laws and actions are the very tools digging them deeper to claim otherwise is to ignore the bulldozed homes the overcrowded hospital wards the imprisoned activists and the millions of children for whom the promise of india remains a distant empty dream
